_about: AI risk / AI benefit ratings written by Claude in chat. risk: how much AI could replace, cheapen or route around what the company sells (1 low - 10 high). benefit: how much AI demand or AI use helps it (1 little - 10 major). Loaded into scr_ai with scripts/load-ai-ratings.mjs (prints the SQL).

ALGM.summary: Magnetic sensors and power chips for cars and factories; AI is a modest new market, not a threat.
risk_reasons: Sells physical chips designed into cars and machines for years; AI can't substitute the part
Chip design tools with AI help rivals too, so design speed is less of an edge over time
benefit_reasons: Current sensors and power chips for data-centre servers and cooling are a growing market
Robotics and automation use more motor-control sensors
Most revenue is still cars and industry, so AI is a minor driver

AMZN.summary: AWS rents the computing AI runs on and Amazon uses AI across retail and ads; the main AI risk is AI shopping assistants bypassing its store.
risk_reasons: AI shopping agents could choose products across stores, weakening Amazon's search and ad position
Competing AI clouds (Microsoft, Google) can win the largest AI customers
benefit_reasons: AWS sells the computing, storage and own chips (Trainium) that AI needs
Warehouse robotics and AI planning cut fulfilment costs
Ads and product search improve with AI recommendations

ASML.summary: Sole maker of EUV lithography machines needed for every leading-edge AI chip.
risk_reasons: Builds the most complex machines in industry; AI cannot replace the hardware or its supply chain
Customer concentration means an AI-chip spending slowdown would hit orders
benefit_reasons: Every advanced AI chip (NVIDIA, TSMC, memory) is printed on its EUV machines
More AI chips and denser memory need more and newer EUV tools
AI demand pulls forward next-generation High-NA EUV sales

AVGO.summary: Designs custom AI chips for Google, Meta and others and sells the network chips that link AI clusters; its software arm (VMware) is less tied to AI.
risk_reasons: Big customers could take custom-chip design in-house over time
VMware's per-seat infrastructure software faces some pressure as AI changes how data centres are run
benefit_reasons: Custom AI accelerators (Google TPU and others) are its fastest-growing business
Its Ethernet switch chips connect the GPUs in AI data centres
AI cluster build-outs are a multi-year spending wave

AXON.summary: TASERs, body cameras and police evidence software; AI turns its huge video archive into new paid products.
risk_reasons: Hardware plus long government contracts and evidence systems are hard for AI startups to displace
AI report-writing rivals could compete for parts of the software budget
benefit_reasons: Sells AI tools (Draft One report writing, real-time translation, video search) as add-ons
Owns years of police video and records that AI features are built on
AI raises software revenue per officer on an existing customer base

BWXT.summary: Builds nuclear reactors for US Navy submarines and carriers and nuclear fuel components; AI data-centre power demand is an indirect boost.
risk_reasons: Sole-source naval reactor supplier under government security rules; AI cannot replace it
Little exposure to software or labour that AI would automate
benefit_reasons: AI data centres need firm power, lifting interest in nuclear and small reactors
Fuel and component work for commercial nuclear could grow with that demand
Defence work, its core, is unrelated to AI

CAT.summary: Mining, construction and power-generation equipment; data centres are a large new buyer of its generators and turbines.
risk_reasons: Heavy machinery and its global dealer and service network are not something AI replaces
Autonomous-mining software could let new entrants compete on the technology layer
benefit_reasons: Backup generators and gas turbines (Solar Turbines) are in high demand for AI data centres
Autonomous haul trucks and AI maintenance services raise its service revenue
Most revenue still depends on construction and mining cycles

FTNT.summary: Network security hardware and software; AI both arms attackers (more demand) and helps rival security platforms.
risk_reasons: AI-native security platforms could win share from appliance-based firewalls
AI coding lowers the cost of building competing security products
benefit_reasons: AI-powered attacks raise demand for security spending
Its own chips and AI threat detection run inside its firewalls
AI data centres need high-speed network security appliances

GD.summary: Submarines, combat vehicles, Gulfstream jets and government IT services; little AI effect except in its IT unit.
risk_reasons: Submarines, tanks and business jets cannot be replaced by AI
Its IT services arm (GDIT) does labour-heavy government work that AI could shrink
benefit_reasons: GDIT can sell AI projects to government agencies
AI-enabled defence systems add content to its platforms
Core shipbuilding and Gulfstream revenue are unrelated to AI

GEV.summary: Gas turbines, grid equipment and wind; AI data-centre power demand has filled its turbine order book for years.
risk_reasons: Builds turbines and grid hardware; AI cannot replace them
If AI data-centre plans are cut back, part of the order surge could fade
benefit_reasons: Gas turbines are sold out for years largely because of data-centre power demand
Grid equipment (transformers, switchgear) is needed to connect new AI capacity
Pricing on new turbine orders has risen with demand

GOOG.summary: Builds leading AI models (Gemini) and its own AI chips, and runs Google Cloud; AI chat assistants are the main threat to Search ads.
risk_reasons: AI assistants answering questions directly could reduce Search queries and ad clicks, its main profit source
AI answers may earn less per query than classic ad links
benefit_reasons: Gemini models, TPU chips and Google Cloud put it among the main AI suppliers
AI improves YouTube and ad targeting
Owns huge data, distribution (Android, Chrome) and computing to deploy AI at low cost

HONA.summary: Honeywell's aerospace business (engines, avionics, flight controls), listed separately; AI adds some avionics and data-centre cooling demand.
risk_reasons: Certified aircraft parts and decades-long aftermarket contracts can't be replaced by AI
AI could cut the value of some cockpit and maintenance software over time
benefit_reasons: AI-based flight and maintenance software adds to avionics sales
Defence autonomy programmes need its navigation and control systems
Most growth still comes from air travel and defence budgets

KLAC.summary: Leader in chip inspection and measurement machines; advanced AI chips need far more inspection steps.
risk_reasons: Specialised machines with decades of process data; AI does not replace them
Depends on chipmakers' spending, which can drop if AI demand slows
benefit_reasons: Leading-edge AI chips and advanced packaging need many more inspection steps
High-bandwidth memory for AI raises demand for its tools
Holds over half the inspection market, so it captures most of that growth

LLY.summary: Drug maker led by obesity and diabetes drugs; AI speeds drug discovery but also helps rivals.
risk_reasons: Patented drugs and large manufacturing can't be replaced by AI
AI-discovered drugs could bring new competitors to market faster
benefit_reasons: AI shortens drug discovery and trial design, cutting R&D cost and time
Large investments in AI computing for research (with NVIDIA)
Sales depend on its drugs, not AI

LRCX.summary: Leader in etch and deposition machines; high-bandwidth memory and advanced chips for AI need more of its tools.
risk_reasons: Complex manufacturing equipment that AI cannot replace
Exposed to swings in chipmakers' spending and China export limits
benefit_reasons: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI chips uses many etch and deposition steps where it leads
3D chip structures and advanced packaging increase its tool demand
AI data centres drive memory and logic capacity spending

MCD.summary: Global burger chain, mostly franchised; AI helps ordering and labour costs at the margin.
risk_reasons: Physical restaurants and a brand; AI cannot replace a meal
AI-driven delivery apps could take a larger share of the customer relationship
benefit_reasons: AI drive-thru ordering and kitchen scheduling can cut labour costs for franchisees
Loyalty app personalisation can lift visits
AI is a small lever compared with menu, price and traffic

META.summary: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp ads; AI improves ad targeting and content ranking, while spending on AI computing is very large.
risk_reasons: AI assistants could pull time and attention away from social feeds
Heavy AI spending may not earn a return if its models trail rivals
benefit_reasons: AI ranking and ad targeting have raised engagement and ad prices
AI tools let advertisers create and target ads automatically
Owns the data and 3+ billion users to deploy AI features at scale

MSFT.summary: Azure cloud, Office and Windows; a main seller of AI computing and AI assistants, but per-seat Office software could be pressured.
risk_reasons: If AI agents replace office workers, per-user Office 365 licences could shrink
AI coding tools make it cheaper for rivals to build competing software
benefit_reasons: Azure rents AI computing and hosts OpenAI models
Copilot AI add-ons raise revenue per Office and GitHub user
Has the enterprise customer base to sell AI to quickly

NFLX.summary: Streaming subscription service; AI cuts production costs for Netflix but also for every rival and for AI-generated video.
risk_reasons: AI-generated video could flood viewers with cheap content competing for time
Lower production costs for everyone weaken the edge of its big content budget
benefit_reasons: AI recommendations keep viewers engaged
AI can lower dubbing, effects and production costs
Large subscriber base spreads AI tool costs widely

NOC.summary: Stealth bombers, missiles, space systems and nuclear deterrent work; AI adds to autonomy and space programmes.
risk_reasons: Classified weapons and space programmes can't be replaced by AI
AI-native defence startups could win newer drone and software contracts
benefit_reasons: Autonomous systems and AI-enabled sensors add to defence budgets it competes for
Space and missile-defence programmes use more AI processing
Core revenue tied to long government programmes, not AI

NOW.summary: Workflow software for IT and corporate departments, priced mostly per user; AI agents both threaten seat counts and are its main new product.
risk_reasons: AI agents could cut the number of human users that its per-seat pricing relies on
AI coding makes custom-built or rival workflow tools cheaper
benefit_reasons: Sells AI agents (Now Assist) on top of its existing workflows at higher prices
Holds the company data and processes AI agents need to act on
Deep links into IT operations make it hard to remove

NVDA.summary: Makes the GPUs and networking that most AI is trained and run on.
risk_reasons: Customers' own chips (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium) and AMD could take share
Revenue depends heavily on a few large customers' AI spending
benefit_reasons: Data-centre AI chips are most of its revenue and profit
CUDA software keeps developers on its chips
Sells complete AI systems (GPUs, networking, software)

SNOW.summary: Cloud data warehouse charging by usage; AI raises data processing but cloud providers and AI tools compete directly.
risk_reasons: AI tools could let customers query data without a dedicated data platform
Cloud giants bundle cheaper data and AI services
benefit_reasons: AI projects need clean company data, which is what it stores
Usage-based pricing grows as AI workloads run on its platform
Sells AI features (Cortex) on top of stored data

SNPS.summary: Chip-design software and IP, a two-player market with Cadence; AI chips raise design demand and AI is built into its tools.
risk_reasons: AI-native design tools or chip designers building their own could weaken the duopoly over time
Seat-based licences could shrink if AI makes engineers more productive
benefit_reasons: Every new AI chip is designed and verified with its software
AI design assistants (Synopsys.ai) are sold as premium add-ons
Chip complexity from AI raises verification and simulation spending

SOLS.summary: Honeywell's former materials unit: refrigerants, specialty fibres and electronic materials; AI chip and data-centre cooling demand gives a modest lift.
risk_reasons: Physical chemicals and materials with plant and patent barriers; AI does not replace them
AI-driven materials discovery could help rivals develop alternatives
benefit_reasons: Electronic materials (metal targets for chip making) benefit from AI chip output
Data-centre cooling needs refrigerants and coolants
Most revenue is refrigerants and industrial materials, so AI is a small part

SPCX.summary: Rocket launches and Starlink satellite internet; AI is not a threat and adds some demand for satellite connectivity and space data.
risk_reasons: Reusable rockets and a satellite network cannot be replaced by AI
AI could help rival launch companies design faster, slightly reducing its lead
benefit_reasons: AI devices and remote sites need connectivity Starlink sells
AI improves rocket and satellite operations
Most value comes from launch and Starlink growth, not AI

SPGI.summary: Credit ratings, S&P indices, financial data and analytics; ratings and indices are protected, but data and research products are exposed to AI.
risk_reasons: AI tools can summarise filings and build analytics, competing with its paid data and research products
Investors may need fewer analyst seats on its data terminals
benefit_reasons: Credit ratings are required by regulation and AI can't issue them
S&P index licensing is unaffected by AI
Its proprietary data becomes more valuable as AI training and input

TDG.summary: Sole-source aircraft parts with high-margin replacement sales; AI has little effect either way.
risk_reasons: Certified, sole-source aircraft parts can't be replaced by AI
AI-based maintenance planning could make airlines' parts buying slightly more efficient
benefit_reasons: Some AI use in manufacturing and pricing
Growth depends on air travel and defence, not AI

TER.summary: Chip-testing machines and industrial robots; AI chips and high-bandwidth memory need far more testing time.
risk_reasons: Physical test equipment with long customer qualification; AI doesn't replace it
Its robotics unit faces cheaper rivals
benefit_reasons: AI processors and HBM memory require longer and more complex testing
Custom AI chips from cloud companies add new test customers
Robots (Universal Robots) benefit from AI-driven automation

TMO.summary: Lab instruments, consumables and drug-development services; AI-driven research needs more lab output.
risk_reasons: Lab equipment, consumables and manufacturing services can't be replaced by AI
AI could reduce the number of lab experiments needed in some research
benefit_reasons: AI drug discovery creates more candidates to test and make
Supplies the data-generating instruments AI biology relies on
AI improves its own clinical trial services efficiency

TSM.summary: Makes almost all of the world's leading AI chips for NVIDIA, Apple, Broadcom and others.
risk_reasons: Leading-edge chip factories cost tens of billions; AI does not replace them
Taiwan geopolitical risk and customer concentration in AI
benefit_reasons: Manufactures nearly every advanced AI chip, from NVIDIA GPUs to custom accelerators
AI chips need its most advanced, highest-priced processes and packaging (CoWoS)
AI demand is its fastest-growing revenue line

V.summary: Card payments network; AI shopping agents still need a trusted way to pay, which Visa is building.
risk_reasons: AI agents could route payments through cheaper rails such as bank transfers or stablecoins
Network effects and bank relationships make it hard to bypass today
benefit_reasons: AI fraud detection lowers losses on its network
Builds payment credentials for AI shopping agents
More online and agent-driven spending raises card volume

VEEV.summary: Cloud software for drug companies (sales, clinical, regulatory), priced largely per user; AI could cut user numbers but Veeva holds regulated industry data.
risk_reasons: AI could reduce sales and clinical staff, lowering per-user licences
AI coding makes industry-specific software easier to build
benefit_reasons: Regulated clinical and compliance data makes switching risky for customers
Sells AI agents inside its life-sciences software
Industry data sets are useful inputs for AI

WMT.summary: World's largest retailer; AI improves inventory, pricing and automation, while AI shopping agents could favour the cheapest seller.
risk_reasons: AI shopping agents comparing prices could reduce store loyalty
Its stores and supply chain are physical, so AI cannot replace them
benefit_reasons: AI forecasting and warehouse automation cut inventory and labour costs
Growing ads business benefits from AI targeting
Scale lets it spread AI investments over huge sales
